what: MEDIUM (RQ-20260927-003, discovered 2026-09-27): the ETHUSDT/1h leg of scripts/research/exit_head_prop_swap_feasibility.py (config-exact trend_donchian_eth_prop params: donchian/atr_stop_mult/trail_mult 3.5/tp_r 6.0, ~5y of 1h-resampled data) is far too CPU-heavy for ad-hoc synchronous OR even detached dispatch on the shared 1-OCPU trainer (158.178.209.121): after fixing a real correctness bug in the same session (the driver silently skipped the resolver's resample flag, so both PRIOR dispatches ran on raw 5-minute bars instead of 1h -- ~12x the intended bar count, fixed in PR for branch claude/w6-prop-o2-exit-head), a CORRECTED single-leg (ETH only, no retrain) detached run still had not finished after 68+ minutes of sustained ~97% CPU (n=1 ps sample, taken once near the end of the 68-minute window; measured via `ps`: ELAPSED 4160s, TIME 01:07:20, RSS 279MB -- genuinely progressing, not hung/stuck). For comparison, RQ-20260927-002's BTCUSDT 3-FOLD WALK-FORWARD RETRAIN (materially more compute: three LightGBM training runs plus replay) completed in ~20 minutes on the same box. Compounding factor observed but not isolated: a recurring ~hourly `drift_retrain` heavy job held runtime_logs/trainer/.heavy.lock three separate times during this session's polling window (13:02, 14:02, 15:03 UTC) -- per src/utils/trainer_heavy_lock.py's own docstring a per-strategy research backtest is deliberately NOT queued behind that lock (light jobs run direct), so it competed for the single CPU rather than being serialized. Whether the dominant cost is CPU contention, an algorithmic inefficiency specific to this leg's trade population (long trail_mult/tp_r -> unusually long average hold, which both run_backtest's bar-by-bar loop and exit_head_replay.replay_trade's per-trade forward bar-scan pay for per bar held), or both, was NOT isolated this session -- filed rather than guessed. Consequence: RQ-20260927-003 cannot be answered (both legs) within a normal trainer-vm-diag dispatch window even with the resample bug fixed; research/queue/RQ-20260927-003.yaml's result reads producer_failed for a second time, now for a CONFIRMED rather than speculative reason.
